note: Deterministic ingredient conflict rules. Families use 'a|b' keyword matching. Evidence grades: A strong RCT/guideline, B consistent studies, C mechanistic/small studies, D expert consensus or debunked folklore kept for transparency.

rules.mechanism: Benzoyl peroxide is a strong oxidizer that can degrade retinol and its esters when layered at the same time, and the pair is strongly drying together.
rules.source: AAD acne management guidelines; Journal of Drugs in Dermatology retinoid stability reviews
rules.resolution: Keep benzoyl peroxide in the morning and the retinoid at night.
rules.userCopy: These two cancel each other out when layered and double the dryness.

rules.mechanism: AHAs lower the pH barrier while retinoids speed up cell turnover; layering them multiplies irritation and peeling risk.
rules.source: AAD retinoid tolerability guidance; dermatology irritation-stacking reviews
rules.resolution: Use the acid on exfoliation nights and the retinoid on retinoid nights.
rules.userCopy: An acid plus a retinoid at once is a fast track to flaky, angry skin.

rules.mechanism: Salicylic acid degreases the barrier the same night a retinoid asks it to renew, which compounds irritation for most people.
rules.source: AAD retinoid tolerability guidance; acne combination-therapy reviews
rules.resolution: Schedule the salicylic acid product on exfoliation nights, away from the retinoid.
rules.userCopy: Salicylic acid and retinoids on the same night usually means stinging.

rules.mechanism: Two retinoid products stack the same active pathway, multiplying irritation without improving results.
rules.resolution: Keep only one retinoid product in tonight's routine and park the other in the cabinet.
rules.userCopy: You have two retinoid products — one is plenty.

rules.mechanism: Over-the-counter retinoids and prescription tretinoin compete for the same receptors and stack irritation.
rules.resolution: Run only the tretinoin tonight; keep the other retinoid for recovery nights only if your skin agrees.
rules.userCopy: Two retinoids at once — pick one tonight.

rules.mechanism: Adapalene plus another retinoid doubles retinoid exposure and usually exceeds tolerability.
rules.resolution: Keep adapalene as the only retinoid in tonight's routine.
rules.userCopy: Two retinoids at once — keep just the adapalene tonight.

rules.mechanism: Sulfur is drying and keratolytic; combined with a retinoid it commonly causes tightness and flaking.
rules.resolution: Use the sulfur product in the morning or on recovery nights.
rules.userCopy: Sulfur plus a retinoid is very drying on the same night.

rules.mechanism: The pH each ingredient prefers differs; old advice says they destabilize each other, though modern formulations mostly tolerate it.
rules.resolution: The common fix is vitamin C in the morning, retinoid at night.
rules.userCopy: Vitamin C works best in the morning; the retinoid owns the night.

rules.mechanism: High-alcohol products strip lipids the retinoid-renewed barrier needs, adding stinging and dryness.
rules.resolution: Apply the retinoid first, buffer with moisturizer, and keep alcohol-heavy layers for non-retinoid nights.
rules.userCopy: That alcohol-heavy product will sting on retinoid nights.

rules.mechanism: Enzyme exfoliants dissolve protein bonds while retinoids accelerate turnover; together they over-exfoliate.
rules.resolution: Save the enzyme product for exfoliation nights without the retinoid.
rules.userCopy: Enzyme exfoliation and retinoids on one night is over-exfoliation.

rules.mechanism: Peels containing TCA resurface aggressively; retinoids must be paused around peel use to avoid burns.
rules.resolution: Pause the retinoid for at least a week around any peel product.
rules.userCopy: Never layer a retinoid with a peel product.

rules.mechanism: PHAs are the gentlest exfoliants but still add turnover on top of a retinoid.
rules.resolution: Fine for most; if your skin is reactive, alternate nights.
rules.userCopy: PHA is gentle, but with a retinoid sensitive skin may still complain.

rules.mechanism: Azelaic acid is usually well tolerated with retinoids but the pair can sting when both are new to your skin.
rules.resolution: Introduce slowly: azelaic acid in the morning, retinoid at night.
rules.userCopy: Azelaic acid and retinoids can team up — start slow.

rules.mechanism: Unlike retinol, adapalene is chemically stable with benzoyl peroxide — the two are even co-formulated in prescription acne gels.
rules.resolution: Safe to use together; add moisturizer if dryness shows up.
rules.userCopy: Adapalene and benzoyl peroxide are a proven pair — just watch for dryness.

rules.mechanism: AHAs plus adapalene stack exfoliation and barrier stress.
rules.resolution: Alternate: acid on exfoliation nights, adapalene on retinoid nights.
rules.userCopy: Split the acid and adapalene across different nights.

rules.mechanism: Salicylic acid plus adapalene compounds dryness for most users.
rules.resolution: Use salicylic acid in the morning and adapalene at night.
rules.userCopy: Salicylic acid mornings, adapalene nights.

rules.mechanism: Two adapalene products double the dose with no added benefit.
rules.resolution: Keep one adapalene product in tonight's routine.
rules.userCopy: One adapalene is enough tonight.

rules.mechanism: Two prescription-strength retinoids together far exceed standard dosing.
rules.resolution: Choose one prescription retinoid per night as directed by your prescriber.
rules.userCopy: Pick one prescription retinoid — never both.

rules.mechanism: Sulfur's drying effect stacks with adapalene-related dryness.
rules.resolution: Keep sulfur for mornings or recovery nights.
rules.userCopy: Sulfur makes adapalene dryness worse on the same night.

rules.mechanism: Classic teaching says benzoyl peroxide oxidizes tretinoin; modern gel combos are stable, but separate application remains the safe default.
rules.source: Tretinoin stability studies; combination gel trials
rules.resolution: Benzoyl peroxide in the morning, tretinoin at night.
rules.userCopy: BPO mornings, tretinoin nights — the safe split.

rules.mechanism: AHAs compound the peeling and sensitivity tretinoin already causes.
rules.resolution: Acids go on exfoliation nights only; never with tretinoin.
rules.userCopy: Skip acids on tretinoin nights.

rules.mechanism: Salicylic acid plus tretinoin is a classic over-drying stack.
rules.resolution: Use salicylic acid in the morning.
rules.userCopy: Salicylic acid mornings, tretinoin nights.

rules.mechanism: Doubling tretinoin doubles irritation with no added efficacy.
rules.resolution: One tretinoin product per night.
rules.userCopy: One tretinoin is enough tonight.

rules.mechanism: Sulfur's keratolytic drying stacks with tretinoid dryness.
rules.resolution: Use sulfur in the morning instead.
rules.userCopy: Keep sulfur away from tretinoin nights.

rules.mechanism: Alcohol-heavy layers sting freshly tretinoin-treated skin.
rules.resolution: Buffer with moisturizer or move the alcohol-heavy product to mornings.
rules.userCopy: Alcohol-heavy products sting on tretinoin nights.

rules.mechanism: Enzyme exfoliation on tretinoin-treated skin is a strong over-exfoliation risk.
rules.resolution: Enzymes on their own nights, never with tretinoin.
rules.userCopy: Enzyme masks and tretinoin don't share a night.

rules.mechanism: Peel products and tretinoin together can cause chemical burns.
rules.resolution: Pause tretinoin around any peel use.
rules.userCopy: Pause tretinoin around peels.

rules.mechanism: Vitamin C prefers a low pH in the morning; layering with tretinoin is tolerated by many but can sting.
rules.resolution: Vitamin C in the morning, tretinoin at night.
rules.userCopy: The classic split: vitamin C AM, tretinoin PM.

rules.mechanism: This pair is often combined intentionally (Kligman's formula) under medical supervision.
rules.resolution: Fine if your prescriber set it up; otherwise alternate nights.
rules.userCopy: Tretinoin and hydroquinone are often prescribed together — follow your prescriber.

rules.mechanism: Benzoyl peroxide plus glycolic or lactic acid is aggressively drying for most skin.
rules.resolution: Run the acid on exfoliation nights, BPO on other days.
rules.userCopy: BPO and acids together over-dry most people.

rules.mechanism: Commonly paired on purpose in acne care, but the combo dries some people out.
rules.resolution: Fine to combine; add moisturizer if tightness appears.
rules.userCopy: BPO and salicylic acid often team up — just watch for dryness.

rules.mechanism: Benzoyl peroxide oxidizes vitamin C on contact, weakening both.
rules.source: Vitamin C oxidation chemistry; cosmetic chemistry literature
rules.resolution: Vitamin C in the morning, benzoyl peroxide later or on alternate days.
rules.userCopy: BPO oxidizes vitamin C — keep them apart.

rules.mechanism: Strong oxidizers destabilize copper peptide complexes.
rules.resolution: Use the copper peptide serum at a different time of day than BPO.
rules.userCopy: BPO breaks down copper peptides — separate them.

rules.mechanism: The old 'niacinamide plus BPO flushes' concern came from raw-powder heating during compounding, not finished products.
rules.source: Niacinamide stability reviews (myth debunked for finished products)
rules.resolution: Safe to layer in modern products.
rules.userCopy: Niacinamide and BPO are fine together in finished products.

rules.mechanism: Benzoyl peroxide's oxidation can degrade peptide chains before they do their job.
rules.resolution: Keep peptides for recovery nights.
rules.userCopy: Peptides don't survive BPO — separate them.

rules.mechanism: Two benzoyl peroxide products double irritation risk without clearing skin faster.
rules.resolution: Use only one benzoyl peroxide product today.
rules.userCopy: One BPO product is enough today.

rules.mechanism: Two drying acne actives stacked together commonly cause flaking.
rules.resolution: Alternate: sulfur mornings, BPO evenings.
rules.userCopy: Sulfur plus BPO is a dryness double-hit.

rules.mechanism: BPO oxidation can denature enzymes before they exfoliate.
rules.resolution: Enzyme products go on nights without BPO.
rules.userCopy: Enzymes and BPO fight each other — separate them.

rules.mechanism: Two AHAs stack free-acid concentration and raise over-exfoliation risk.
rules.resolution: Pick one AHA product per night.
rules.userCopy: Two AHAs is double-dosing exfoliation — pick one.

rules.mechanism: AHA and BHA together push total exfoliation past what most barriers tolerate nightly.
rules.resolution: Alternate acid types across nights, or use one in AM and one in PM only if your skin is resilient.
rules.userCopy: AHA plus BHA on one night is heavy exfoliation.

rules.mechanism: Both prefer low pH, but layering can spike stinging on sensitive skin.
rules.resolution: Vitamin C in the morning, acids at night.
rules.userCopy: Vitamin C mornings, acid nights keeps stinging away.

rules.mechanism: Acidic pH destabilizes copper peptide complexes.
rules.resolution: Copper peptides on recovery nights, acids on exfoliation nights.
rules.userCopy: Acids break down copper peptides — use different nights.

rules.mechanism: Old flushing worries came from raw materials, not finished products; most skin handles the pair.
rules.resolution: Safe for most; if flushing occurs, separate them.
rules.userCopy: Niacinamide and acids are fine together for most people.

rules.mechanism: Both are mild; stacked they can tingle on reactive skin.
rules.resolution: Alternate if you feel stinging.
rules.userCopy: Azelaic acid and AHAs can tingle together on sensitive skin.

rules.mechanism: Sulfur plus acids is a strong drying combination.
rules.resolution: Sulfur mornings, acids nights.
rules.userCopy: Sulfur and acids together dry skin fast.

rules.mechanism: Low pH environments hydrolyze many signal peptides.
rules.resolution: Peptides on recovery nights.
rules.userCopy: Acids shorten peptide shelf-life on your skin — separate them.

rules.mechanism: AHAs enhance penetration of hydroquinone, increasing irritation risk.
rules.resolution: Fine under dermatologist guidance; otherwise alternate.
rules.userCopy: Acids boost hydroquinone penetration — go slow.

rules.mechanism: Alcohol-heavy layers sting freshly exfoliated skin.
rules.resolution: Apply the acid first and buffer, or move the alcohol-heavy product to mornings.
rules.userCopy: Alcohol-heavy products sting after acids.

rules.mechanism: Chemical and enzymatic exfoliation stacked is a high over-exfoliation risk.
rules.resolution: Pick one exfoliation method per night.
rules.userCopy: Two exfoliation methods in one night is too much.

rules.mechanism: AHAs before or after a TCA peel significantly raise burn risk.
rules.resolution: Pause acids around peel use.
rules.userCopy: Never layer acids with a TCA peel product.

rules.mechanism: PHA adds to total acid load, though gently.
rules.resolution: Fine for resilient skin; alternate if reactive.
rules.userCopy: PHA is gentle but still adds to the acid load.

rules.mechanism: Two salicylate sources stack exfoliation and dryness.
rules.resolution: Keep one BHA product per night.
rules.userCopy: Two salicylic acid products — one is enough.

rules.mechanism: Both are acidic; layering can sting but is not destabilizing.
rules.resolution: Vitamin C mornings, BHA nights.
rules.userCopy: Vitamin C mornings keeps BHA stinging away.

rules.mechanism: Salicylic acid's low pH destabilizes copper peptides.
rules.resolution: Copper peptides on recovery nights.
rules.userCopy: BHA and copper peptides don't mix well.

rules.mechanism: Mild pair that can tingle on reactive skin.
rules.resolution: Alternate if stinging shows up.
rules.userCopy: BHA plus azelaic acid can tingle on sensitive skin.

rules.mechanism: Two drying keratolytics stacked.
rules.resolution: Sulfur mornings, BHA nights.
rules.userCopy: Sulfur plus BHA is a dryness stack.

rules.mechanism: Low pH plus keratolysis reduces peptide performance.
rules.resolution: Peptides on recovery nights.
rules.userCopy: Keep peptides away from BHA nights.

rules.mechanism: Stacked exfoliation modalities.
rules.resolution: One exfoliation method per night.
rules.userCopy: Enzymes and BHA double up on exfoliation.

rules.mechanism: Salicylic acid before a TCA peel raises complications risk.
rules.resolution: Pause BHA around peel use.
rules.userCopy: Pause BHA around TCA peels.

rules.mechanism: BHA increases hydroquinone penetration somewhat.
rules.resolution: Alternate nights unless directed otherwise.
rules.userCopy: Go slow combining BHA with hydroquinone.

rules.mechanism: L-ascorbic acid destabilizes copper peptide complexes in vitro, reducing both.
rules.source: In-vitro copper peptide and ascorbic acid interaction studies
rules.resolution: Vitamin C in the morning, copper peptides at night.
rules.userCopy: Vitamin C and copper peptides deactivate each other — split AM/PM.

rules.mechanism: The flushing myth came from unstable raw materials in the 1960s; finished modern products are fine together.
rules.resolution: Safe to layer; separate only if you notice flushing.
rules.userCopy: Vitamin C and niacinamide are fine together in modern formulas.

rules.mechanism: Two vitamin C products double sting risk without doubling brightening.
rules.resolution: Keep one vitamin C product per morning.
rules.userCopy: One vitamin C is enough.

rules.mechanism: Both are acidic but mild; sensitive skin may tingle.
rules.resolution: Alternate if stinging occurs.
rules.userCopy: Vitamin C plus PHA is usually fine — alternate if tingly.

rules.mechanism: Mild acids may slowly destabilize copper complexes.
rules.resolution: Copper peptides on recovery nights works best.
rules.userCopy: PHAs are gentle on copper peptides but different nights is safer.

rules.mechanism: Two sulfur products double dryness.
rules.resolution: One sulfur product per day.
rules.userCopy: One sulfur product is enough today.

rules.mechanism: Stacked enzymatic exfoliation over-thins the barrier.
rules.resolution: One enzyme product per night.
rules.userCopy: One enzyme product per night.

rules.mechanism: Benzoyl peroxide's oxidation can degrade hydroquinone.
rules.resolution: Apply at different times of day.
rules.userCopy: BPO can oxidize hydroquinone — different times of day.
